# Section I

## Part A – 20 marks

Use the multiple-choice answer sheet for Questions 1–20.

### Question 1

Which of the following is an industrial use of ammonia?

A. As a catalyst in the Haber process

B. As a reagent in the production of fertilisers

C. As a catalyst in the manufacture of explosives

D. As a reagent in the treatment of drinking water

### Question 2

Which row of the table correctly matches the chemical additive with its main function in a water treatment plant?

|     | Additive | Function |
|-----|----------|----------|
| A.  | Chlorine | Kills microorganisms |
| B.  | Fluoride | Reduces turbidity |
| C.  | \ce{Fe^3+} | Minimises tooth decay |
| D.  | HCl | Increases the pH of the water |

### Question 3

An esterification reaction is to be performed.

Which of the following substances, when added, would increase the yield of the product?

A. Water

B. Boiling chips

C. More alkanol

D. Dilute sulfuric acid

### Question 4

Which of the following greatly enhanced scientific understanding of the effects of trace elements?

A. Improved filtration techniques

B. The development of atomic absorption spectroscopy

C. The creation of new elements in particle accelerators

D. The work of Le Chatelier in describing chemical equilibrium

### Question 5

Cellulose extracted from biomass is able to be used as a raw material in the manufacture of polymers because it

A. is a condensation polymer.

B. is a strong flexible molecule.

C. produces carbon dioxide when burnt.

D. contains a basic carbon-chain structure.

### Question 6

Sodium hydrogen carbonate is often used to clean up large spills of acids and alkalis.

Why is it a suitable chemical for this application?

A. It is diprotic and is readily neutralised.

B. It is amphiprotic, stable and easily handled.

C. It is diprotic and easily cleaned up when neutralised.

D. It is amphiprotic and only small quantities are required.

### Question 8

Which row of the table correctly identifies a major source of an acidic oxide in the atmosphere and the chemical equation for the formation of the oxide?

|     | Source | Equation |
|-----|--------|----------|
| A.  | Volcanoes | \ce{N2(g) + O2(g) -> 2NO(g)} |
| B.  | Mineral smelting | \ce{2ZnS(s) + 3O2(g) -> 2ZnO(s) + 2SO2(g)} |
| C.  | Lightning | \ce{4NO(g) + 3O2(g) + 2H2O(g) -> 4HNO3(aq)} |
| D.  | Incomplete combustion of fuels | \ce{2C8H18(l) + 17O2(g) -> 16CO(g) + 18H2O(g)} |

### Question 12

A silver spoon becomes tarnished over time according to the following reaction.

$$\ce{4Ag(s) + O2(g) + 2H2S(g) -> 2Ag2S(s) + 2H2O(l)}$$

Which row of the table correctly describes this process?

|     | Type of reaction of silver | Change in oxidation state |
|-----|---------------------------|--------------------------|
| A.  | Oxidation | From 0 to +1 |
| B.  | Oxidation | From 0 to +2 |
| C.  | Reduction | From +2 to +1 |
| D.  | Reduction | From +4 to +2 |

Which compound would be most likely to remain in the flask?

A. Pentanol

B. Propyl acetate

C. Pentanoic acid

D. Ethyl propanoate

### Question 15

A solution containing potassium dihydrogen phosphate and potassium hydrogen phosphate is a common laboratory buffer with a pH close to 7.

Which row of the table correctly identifies the chemistry of this buffer?

|     | Buffer equation | Equilibrium shift |  |
|-----|----------------|-------------------|---|
|     |                | Acid is added to the solution | Alkali is added to the solution |
| A.  | \ce{HPO4^2- + H2O <=> PO4^3- + H3O+} | Right | Left |
| B.  | \ce{HPO4^2- + H2O <=> PO4^3- + H3O+} | Left | Right |
| C.  | \ce{H2PO4- + H2O <=> HPO4^2- + H3O+} | Right | Left |
| D.  | \ce{H2PO4- + H2O <=> HPO4^2- + H3O+} | Left | Right |

### Question 16

An investigation was carried out to determine the calcium ion concentration of a 2.0 L sample of tap water. Excess \ce{Na2CO3} was added to the sample. The precipitate was filtered, dried and weighed. The mass of the dried precipitate was 400 mg.

What was the concentration of calcium ions in the sample of tap water?

A. 80 mg L^-1^

B. 160 mg L^-1^

C. 200 mg L^-1^

D. 400 mg L^-1^

### Question 20

The Winkler method is used to determine the amount of dissolved oxygen in a water sample. The procedure involves the following sequence of reactions.

Step 1. \ce{2Mn^2+(aq) + O2(g) + 4OH-(aq) -> 2MnO(OH)2(s)}

Step 2. \ce{MnO(OH)2(s) + 2I-(aq) + 4H+(aq) -> I2(aq) + Mn^2+(aq) + 3H2O(aq)}

Step 3. \ce{I2(aq) + 2S2O3^2-(aq) -> 2I-(aq) + S4O6^2-(aq)}

When a 5.00 L sample of water was analysed using the Winkler method, a total of $4.00 \times 10^{-3}$ mol of thiosulfate (\ce{S2O3^2-}) was required in Step 3.

What concentration of oxygen was present in the original sample?

A. 3.20 mg L^-1^

B. 6.40 mg L^-1^

C. 12.8 mg L^-1^

D. 32.0 mg L^-1^

### Question 28 (8 marks)

A camp stove using butane as a fuel was used to heat a pot of water inside a small tent. Poisonous carbon monoxide (CO) gas can be released from these stoves.

![Camp stove diagram showing clearance height](images/q28-camp-stove.png){width=40%}

An investigation was carried out to determine the carbon monoxide concentration in the tent when the clearance height of the pot above the flame was altered. The results are shown in the table.

| Clearance height (mm) | 35 | 40 | 45 | 50 |
|----------------------|----|----|----|----|
| CO concentration (ppm) | 120 | 87 | 50 | 18 |

**(a)** Construct a graph of the data on the grid. **(3 marks)**

![Graph grid](images/q28-graph-grid.png){width=80%}

**(b)** Air containing a CO concentration above 30 ppm is considered unsafe to breathe. **(1 mark)**

What is the minimum clearance height at which the pot should be placed?

\vspace{2cm}

**(c)** Increasing the clearance height decreases the efficiency of the stove according to the following table. **(4 marks)**

| Clearance height (mm) | 35 | 40 | 45 | 50 |
|----------------------|----|----|----|----|
| Efficiency (%) | 90 | 70 | 50 | 30 |

A bushwalker only has 15.0 g of butane with which to heat 1.0 L of water with a starting temperature of 20°C.

Calculate the highest temperature of the water that could safely be achieved in the tent. (Molar heat of combustion of butane: $\Delta H_c = 2877$ kJ mol^-1^)

\vspace{10cm}

### Question 29 (7 marks)

The concentration of hydrochloric acid in a solution was determined by an acid base titration using a standard solution of sodium carbonate.

**(a)** Explain why sodium carbonate is a suitable compound for preparation of a standard solution. **(2 marks)**

\vspace{4cm}

**(b)** A 25.00 mL sample of 0.1050 mol L^-1^ sodium carbonate solution was added to a conical flask and three drops of methyl orange indicator added. The mixture was titrated with the hydrochloric acid and the following readings were recorded. **(3 marks)**

| Initial burette reading (mL) | Final burette reading (mL) | Titre (mL) |
|------------------------------|---------------------------|-----------|
| 0.00 | 22.00 | 22.00 |
| 22.00 | 43.65 | 21.65 |
| 0.00 | 21.70 | 21.70 |
| 21.70 | 43.30 | 21.60 |

Using the data from the table, calculate the concentration of the hydrochloric acid.

\vspace{8cm}

**(c)** Explain the effect on the calculated concentration of hydrochloric acid if phenolphthalein is used as the indicator instead of methyl orange. **(2 marks)**

\vspace{4cm}

### Question 30 (7 marks)

- the amount of fossil fuels burnt
- atmospheric carbon dioxide levels
- average global air temperature and ocean temperature
- the volume of carbon dioxide dissolved in the oceans.

Analyse the factors that affect the equilibrium between carbon dioxide in the air and carbon dioxide in the oceans. In your answer, make reference to the scientists' observations and include relevant equations. **(7 marks)**

## Question 31 — Industrial Chemistry (25 marks)

**(a)** (i) Use a labelled diagram to show the structure of a soap molecule. **(2 marks)**

\vspace{4cm}

(ii) Explain how soap acts as a cleaning agent. **(3 marks)**

\vspace{6cm}

**(b)** Sulfuric acid is an important industrial chemical.

(i) Relate a property of sulfuric acid to a condition necessary for its safe transport and storage. **(2 marks)**

\vspace{4cm}

(ii) Two first-hand investigations are carried out. One demonstrates the use of sulfuric acid as an oxidising agent and the other demonstrates the use of sulfuric acid as a dehydrating agent. **(4 marks)**

Explain the observations that could be made in these investigations. Include relevant equations in your answer.

\vspace{8cm}

**(c)** (i) Consider the following equilibrium reaction, which is endothermic. **(3 marks)**

$$\ce{[Co(H2O)6]^2+ + 4Cl- <=> [CoCl4]^2- + 6H2O(l)}$$

*Pink solution* $\quad\quad\quad\quad$ *Blue solution*

Justify TWO conditions that could change the colour of the solution from pink to blue.

\vspace{6cm}

(ii) 0.20 moles of hydrogen gas and 0.20 moles of iodine gas were placed in a 1.0 L container and allowed to come to equilibrium. **(4 marks)**

$$\ce{H2(g) + I2(g) <=> 2HI(g)}$$

Determine the equilibrium concentration of HI for this reaction, given that the equilibrium constant, K, is 64.

\vspace{8cm}

**(d)** Explain how the environmental issues associated with the industrial production of sodium hydroxide and sodium carbonate can be addressed. Include chemical equations in your answer. **(7 marks)**

\vspace{12cm}

\newpage

## Question 32 — Shipwrecks, Corrosion and Conservation (25 marks)

**(a)** The diagram shows an electrolytic cell.

![Electrolytic cell diagram](images/q32-electrolytic-cell.png){width=40%}

(i) The equipment shown is being used to investigate the effect of changing the concentration of the electrolyte on the rate of reaction in electrolysis. **(2 marks)**

Identify THREE variables that should be kept constant.

\vspace{4cm}

(ii) Calculate the minimum voltage to drive this cell if the electrolyte is 1.0 mol L^-1^ sodium bromide, assuming the electrodes are inert. **(3 marks)**

\vspace{6cm}

**(b)** A first-hand investigation is to be carried out to compare the rates of corrosion of iron and a form of steel.

(i) Outline a suitable procedure for this investigation. **(2 marks)**

\vspace{4cm}

(ii) Explain the process of rusting. Include relevant half equations in your answer. **(4 marks)**

\vspace{8cm}

**(c)** In 1912, the ship *Titanic* sank in water over 3 km deep. The wreck was discovered in 1985. It was badly corroded and covered in rusticles. On analysis, the rusticles were found to be composed of iron(II) sulfide, iron(II) hydroxide and other related compounds. Silver coins were also found on the shipwreck and were covered in silver sulfide.

(i) Explain how the rusticles were formed. Include relevant half equations in your answer. **(3 marks)**

\vspace{6cm}

(ii) Compare TWO methods for restoring the silver coins. Refer to the underlying chemistry in your answer. **(4 marks)**

\vspace{8cm}

**(d)** Explain how advances in chemistry have led to improvements in the protection of steel ships from corrosion in marine environments. Include a relevant equation in your answer. **(7 marks)**

\vspace{12cm}

\newpage

## Question 33 — The Biochemistry of Movement (25 marks)

**(a)** (i) Identify TWO main stages of cellular respiration and the location in the cell where each occurs. **(2 marks)**

\vspace{4cm}

(ii) Describe the first stage of cellular respiration. **(3 marks)**

\vspace{6cm}

**(b)** The structure of a dipeptide is shown.

![Dipeptide structure](images/q33-dipeptide.png){width=40%}

(i) Draw the structural formulae of the TWO amino acids from which this dipeptide was made. **(2 marks)**

\vspace{6cm}

(ii) Explain how both forces and bonding are responsible for the tertiary structure of a protein. **(4 marks)**

\vspace{8cm}

**(c)** (i) Describe how glucose monomers combine to form a branched glycogen polymer. **(3 marks)**

\vspace{6cm}

(ii) The energy profile in the graph shows the combustion of glucose during cellular respiration. **(4 marks)**

![Energy profile for glucose combustion](images/q33-energy-profile.png){width=60%}

At 25°C and 100 kPa, a running animal consumes a maximum of 3.5 L of oxygen per minute. For a 5-minute run the animal has adequate glucose available from the blood, some of which is mobilised from glycogen stores.

The animal needs 300 kJ of energy to maintain the run aerobically for 5 minutes.

Calculate whether the animal has an adequate supply of oxygen for the run, using data from the energy profile. Support your answer with an equation for cellular respiration.

\vspace{10cm}

**(d)** Explain how the structure of muscle cells relates to the function it performs in both gentle exercise and in sprints. **(7 marks)**

\vspace{12cm}

\newpage

**(a)** (i) The electron configuration of an atom may be represented by using arrows to indicate electrons and boxes to indicate orbitals. For example, the electron configuration of boron would be represented as shown. **(2 marks)**

\vspace{8cm}

\vspace{6cm}

## Question 35 — Forensic Chemistry (25 marks)

**(a)** The diagram is a schematic representation of a mass spectrometer.

![Mass spectrometer diagram](images/q35-mass-spectrometer.png){width=50%}

(i) Name and outline the function of the part labelled A in the diagram. **(2 marks)**

\vspace{4cm}

(ii) Outline the advantages of using mass spectrometry for analysis of a compound. **(3 marks)**

\vspace{6cm}

\vspace{4cm}

\vspace{8cm}
